topic.name: Solving Systems of Equations by Substitution

question.text:
Given the system of equations below, what is the value of $p-q?$

\[ \begin{cases} 3p=15\\[3pt] p+2q=9. \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. It doesn't matter which equation we pick first, so we choose the easiest one. In this case, the first equation looks like the easiest.

Using the first equation, we can isolate $p$ by dividing both sides of the equation by $3\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 3p &=15\\[5pt] p&=5 \end{align*}

If we now substitute $p=5$ into $p+2q=9,$ then we can find the value of $q\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} p+2q&=9\\[5pt] (5)+2q &=9\\[5pt] 2q &=4\\[5pt] q&=2 \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $p=5, \,q=2.$ So,

\[ p-q= 5 - 2 = 3. \]

example.title: Solving a System of Linear Equations Using Substitution

question.text:
Given the system of equations below, what is the value of $a+b?$

\[ \begin{cases} 2b=6a+14\\[3pt] 5b+25=0 \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
We number the equations so that we can refer to them more easily:

\[ \begin{cases} 2b=6a+14 &\qquad \qquad (1)\\[3pt] 5b+25=0. & \qquad \qquad (2) \end{cases} \]

We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. Using equation $(2),$ we can solve for $b$ as follows:

\begin{align} 5b+25&=0\\[5pt] 5b&=-25\\[5pt] b&=-5 \end{align}

Then, we substitute $b=-5$ into equation $(1)$ and solve for $a\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} 2(-5)&=6a+14\\[5pt] -10&=6a+14\\[5pt] -10-14&=6a\\[5pt] 6a &= -24\\[5pt] a&=-4 \end{align}

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $a=-4, \, b=-5.$ So,

\[a + b = -4 + (-5) = -4-5 = -9.\]

example.title: Solving a Challenging System of Linear Equations Using Substitution

question.text: Given the system of equations below, what is the value of $a-b?$ \[ \begin{cases} a=7 \\[3pt] 3a+6b=15 \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. It so happens that the first equation is already solved for $a\mathbin{:}$

\[ a = 7 \]

If we now substitute $a=7$ into $3a+6b=15,$ then we can find the value of $b\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} 3a+6b &= 15\\[5pt] 3(7)+6b &= 15\\[5pt] 6b &= -6\\[5pt] b&=-1 \end{align}

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $a=7, \,b=-1.$ So,

\[ a - b = 7 - (-1) = 7+1= 8. \]
